title: FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models
summary: FrontierReplay replaces fine-grained exact prefix caches for hybrid language models that must split the prefill pass at each mid-prompt checkpoint, instead logging a short window of recurrent-layer inputs during an uncut prefill and replaying them state-only to materialize checkpoints at predictable structural boundaries such as turn ends and branch points. Costs include buffering the logged input window, a custom cross-layer replay kernel, scheduler support for frontier-aware retention, and applicability limited to hybrid architectures with recurrent state; the replay itself is reported at 6-37x cheaper per token than recomputation. The approach can fail if reuse does not actually terminate at predictable structural boundaries (making checkpoint placement wasted), if the deployed models are pure-attention transformers where standard KV prefix caching already suffices, or if kernel and scheduler integration into an existing inference engine is unavailable or immature.
rationale: Prefix caching at structural boundaries is directly relevant to cost-sensitive serving, but the method requires hybrid (attention-plus-recurrent) models and integration with a serving stack, so its benefit depends on the reader's actual model architecture and workload.
technique: Split-free exact prefix caching via state-only replay

claims.statement: FrontierReplay replaces fine-grained exact prefix caches for hybrid language models that must split the prefill pass at each mid-prompt checkpoint, instead logging a short window of recurrent-layer inputs during an uncut prefill and replaying them state-only to materialize checkpoints at predictable structural boundaries such as turn ends and branch points. Costs include buffering the logged input window, a custom cross-layer replay kernel, scheduler support for frontier-aware retention, and applicability limited to hybrid architectures with recurrent state; the replay itself is reported at 6-37x cheaper per token than recomputation. The approach can fail if reuse does not actually terminate at predictable structural boundaries (making checkpoint placement wasted), if the deployed models are pure-attention transformers where standard KV prefix caching already suffices, or if kernel and scheduler integration into an existing inference engine is unavailable or immature.

Lowers median TTFT by 16-89% (up to 8.9x), raises 80% SLO capacity by up to 1.73x, and improves goodput by up to 4.26x versus existing exact caches; up to 1.54x higher goodput than approximate replay without their accuracy loss.
